claims.text: The fare ledger records the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee as already returned to the rider and withheld from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00; the fee_reversed event sits at 2026-08-31T21:11:10+08:00). The driver's filing asks for that reversal to be undone. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and says in terms that NO_ACTION never means 'restore a charge', so the driver cannot succeed on a request that the charge be put back; the only ruling value that could move this money back to the driver is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, which POL-NS-22 licenses only where the fee stands. On this ledger the charge has already been reversed, and the account the driver gives is one this record does not complete, so the present state should be left undisturbed.

I do not contest POL-NS-23 on this record, and I say so rather than stretch it: the trip record carries two in-app chat messages from the driver (17:54:00 and 17:57:10, both delivered and read) and one in-app call placed at 17:58:20, unanswered, ringing 35 s, all before the 18:00:10 cancellation. The contact obligation is met, and the rider's assertion that the driver 'never called me' is not supported by the trip record's own call entry. POL-NS-23 is therefore not a ground on which I ask the fee to be voided.

The rider's account is that the driver was not at the point she set. The arrival check runs only against the trip record's pickup coordinate - the nearest fix is 26.2 m away at 17:53:00, inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius POL-NS-21 sets - and that test does not reach the question the rider actually raises. The trip record carries no registered pickup points for the venue, the chat log carries no rider message naming her meeting point, and the driver's own messages name only the 'Hall 2 taxi and private hire pick-up bay, lane 3'. Nothing in this file ties that bay to the point the rider set, and the two may not be treated as the same place from general geography. Whether the driver presented himself where the rider was told to wait is thus a fact the rules need and this record cannot establish; under POL-GEN-26 the case should go to a human reviewer with the amount held rather than collected from the rider.

I disclose at once that the one third-party artifact in this file is impaired: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05061-01 is MISSING, carries issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, has payload null and weight 0.0. Under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact, so it cannot be used either way; what remains is that every account supporting the driver - trip record, chat log, fare ledger and the trace itself - comes from the platform's own systems or the driver's own device, and nothing independent of them puts the driver at the meeting point the rider says she set.

The only profile field the no-show policy allows as a ground points away from any suggestion of repeat conduct by this rider: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, well below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so the repeat no-show referral is not engaged even on the driver's own version of events, and nothing in the profile can be used to establish a fact about this trip.

claims.text: Arrival at the pickup is established on the platform's own record and corroborated by the trace: the trip record shows driver_arrived at 17:53:40 near the registered pickup point VEN-EXPO-H2, and the GPS check finds the nearest fix 26.2 m from the pickup at 17:53:00 with a reported accuracy of 5 m — inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius the category's arrival test sets — with corroborated = true. The driver was at the pickup, and the rider's assertion that he was not is contradicted by the telemetry.

The free wait ran from the driver's arrival and had expired before he cancelled. This is an on-demand trip — trip_record.scheduled_at is null — so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait starts at the driver's arrival of 17:53:40 and ends at 17:58:40. The driver cancelled at 18:00:10, 390 s after arrival and 90 s after the free wait expired. POL-NS-21's precondition for cancelling as a rider no-show is met.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is satisfied in full: the driver sent two in-app chat messages, at 17:54:00 and 17:57:10, and placed an in-app call at 17:58:20 that rang 35 s unanswered — all three before cancelled_at 18:00:10, and the trip record computes obligation_met = true. The rider's statement that the driver 'never called me' is squarely contradicted by the platform's in_app_calls entry for the trip.

The rider's account is not borne out by any artifact here. She says the driver was not at the pickup point she set at the Hall 2 entrance; the driver's trace shows his device stationary at zero speed from 17:53:30 through 18:00:00, roughly 26 m from the pickup coordinates on the trip record, and the chat log records the driver telling her at 17:54:00 that he was 'at the Hall 2 taxi and private hire pick-up bay, lane 3'. Both messages were read (17:54:41 and 17:57:58), and she was pushed 'Your driver has arrived' at 17:53:44. She had every means of reaching the car and did not.

The amount charged is exactly the POL-NS-22 no-show fee of 5.00 SGD, so the fee stands and is the driver's compensation for time and fuel: the ruling must be DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The driver is the filer, and the fare breakdown records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 — the fee was reversed at 21:11:10 after the rider's complaint and withheld from the driver pending review. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves that present state, which here means the driver stays unpaid for a no-show he handled by the book. NO_ACTION is therefore the driver's loss, and only DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 gives him the money the policy awards.

POL-NS-24 (driver no-show, rider may cancel at no charge) has no application to this trip. The rider did not cancel — the record shows cancelled_by = DRIVER and the cancellation reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW — and the driver did not fail to arrive by any deadline: his arrival at 17:53:40 is corroborated by the trace, and with scheduled_at null on this on-demand trip there is no scheduled time plus 5 minutes for him to have missed.

There is no open question to escalate under POL-GEN-26. Every fact POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 need — when the driver arrived, how long he waited, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and what was charged — is carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0. With the contested amount at 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and fraud_flags 0 on both profiles so the 0.95 bar does not apply, the ruling is final under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26.

EV-ADVIS-05061-01 is MISSING — no traffic advisory was attached for this trip — so under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries weight 0.0 and no fact at all (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), and the driver's case does not rest on it: he reached the pickup about eight minutes after accepting and waited out the full free period, so no traffic excuse is needed to justify his conduct.

Nothing on either party's profile can decide this trip. POL-GEN-01 confines profile material to fraud_flags and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d; neither party carries a fraud flag, and every other history field is context only. The determination therefore rests entirely on the trip telemetry set out above, all of it cited.

ruling.explanation: Driver D-25029 filed to restore the 5.00 SGD no-show fee that was refunded to rider R-20704 at 2026-08-31T21:11:10 and withheld from him pending review. On the record, the fee stands and the driver is owed it back. Arrival: the trip record's driver_arrived event is corroborated by the GPS trace — the nearest fix at 17:53:00 is 26.2 m from the registered pickup point VEN-EXPO-H2 with a reported accuracy of 5 m, inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius the arrival test sets — and the trace shows the vehicle stationary there from 17:53:30 to cancellation. Contact (POL-NS-23): the driver sent two in-app messages (17:54:00 and 17:57:10, both delivered and read) and placed an in-app call at 17:58:20 (unanswered, 35 s), all before cancelled_at 18:00:10, so the contact obligation is met and nothing voids the fee under POL-NS-23 or POL-NS-24. The rider's account is not borne out: her statement that the driver 'never called me' is contradicted by the platform's own in_app_calls entry, and her statement that he was not at the point she set is not carried by any artifact — no coordinate, and the trip record carries no registered pickup points; the arrival test's 120 m large-venue radius is precisely the tolerance that covers the difference between the venue's registered point and the bay she describes. Her escalation argument under POL-GEN-26 is therefore rejected: every fact the rules need — when the driver arrived, how long he waited, whether he messaged and called, and what was charged — is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05061-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact, and nothing here rests on it (POL-GEN-02). Fee (POL-NS-22): the amount charged was exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (EV-FARE-05061), so the fee stands and is the driver's compensation for time and fuel; the interim reversal after the rider's complaint is undone. Under POL-GEN-03 the driver filed against the present state, and where the driver is owed the sum back the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carrying the same figure of 5.00 SGD. No referral is produced: the fee equals the 5.00 SGD policy fee so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire, POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise (the driver arrived and attempted contact), and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral is not engaged. Nothing on either profile decides this trip (POL-GEN-01). The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band with no fraud flags, so this ruling is final (POL-NS-26).

ruling.explanation:
To the driver: your claim succeeds. The 5.00 SGD no-show fee was properly charged, so the reversal after the rider's complaint should not stand, and you are owed 5.00 SGD back.

To the rider: the record does not support the account you gave.

What the record shows. The trip record marks the driver's arrival at 17:53:40 at the pickup you booked (Singapore Expo Hall 2, VEN-EXPO-H2), and the driver's GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix, at 17:53:00, sits 26.2 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 5 m, well inside the 120 m arrival radius the no-show policy sets for a large venue. Because this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, the 300 s (5-minute) free wait ran from the driver's arrival, 17:53:40 to 17:58:40. The driver cancelled at 18:00:10 - 390 s after arrival and 90 s after the free wait expired - so the precondition in POL-NS-21 for cancelling as a rider no-show was met.

The contact obligation. The driver also met POL-NS-23: he sent two in-app messages (17:54:00 and 17:57:10, both delivered and read) and placed one in-app call at 17:58:20 that rang 35 s unanswered, all before the cancellation at 18:00:10. Your statement that he never called you is contradicted by the trip record's own call entry, and your statement that he was not at the pickup is contradicted by the trace. On your escalation argument: POL-GEN-26 sends a case to a human only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence is missing or impaired. The fact that matters here - when the driver arrived - is carried by the trip record and the GPS trace, both graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Which particular bay or entrance he stood at is not a fact the rules require; the policy's own arrival test measures against the booked pickup point, and it is met. I therefore reject that ground.

The fee. The amount charged was exactly 5.00 SGD, the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, so the fee stands and is the driver's compensation for time and fuel; because the amount matches, no POL-NS-22 referral is needed. POL-NS-24 does not apply: you did not cancel, the driver did, and he did arrive, so the clause that would refund you in full for a driver no-show is not engaged. POL-NS-23 does not void the fee either, because both contact steps were taken before cancellation.

Other artifacts. The one impaired artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05061-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), carries no fact either way. The repeat no-show referral in POL-NS-25 is not engaged, as the count is below 3. No referral arises on this record.

Outcome. You filed, driver, and the fee should stand, so the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 - the sum returned to you. Confidence is 0.9, above the bar for a 5.00 SGD dispute with no fraud flags on either profile, so this ruling is final.
